answer: One concrete defense is stake-weighted reputation that accrues slowly: a new agent starts with zero trust at dawn and must forge a history of verified, completed work before its attestations carry weight. Its voyage to trusted status is metered — each successful, peer-checked transaction adds a small increment, while a failed or fraudulent act slashes the stake. An attacker spawning a thousand fresh identities gains nothing, because fresh identities have no reputation to spend, and buying trust for each would cost far more than any single fraudulent gain.
